best_for: Reverse engineers, firmware hackers and programmers who need to read binary formats, and who would rather describe a file layout once than decode it by hand at 3 AM.
description:
ImHex is a hex editor for reverse engineers and programmers, written by the developer known as WerWolv. Dark mode is the default, and the project is funded through GitHub Sponsors and Ko-fi, with free tools and credits from JetBrains, SignPath and AWS.

You can patch bytes with unlimited undo, then copy a selection as a C, C++, C#, Rust, Python, Java or JavaScript array, or as a self-contained HTML block. Patches import and export as IPS files, and findings can be saved as a Markdown report. Search covers strings with a set minimum length and encoding, byte sequences and regular expressions. Bookmarks and color rules highlight the parts that matter, and a free web version runs in your browser.

points.title: A language for file layouts
points.text: The built-in Pattern Language is C-like: you write structs, unions, enums and bitfields, and ImHex highlights and decodes the matching bytes. It can show images, audio and 3D models found inside the data.

points.title: More than a hex view
points.text: It has a data inspector, a Capstone-based disassembler for x86, ARM, MIPS, RISC-V and more, a node-based data processor, entropy graphs, hashing, diffing and YARA scans.

points.title: Reads more than files
points.text: Data sources include raw disks, process memory, GDB servers, UDP packets and remote files over SSH and SFTP.

points.title: Needs OpenGL 3
points.text: The interface draws with the GPU and needs OpenGL 3.0 or newer. Windows and macOS also get slower software-rendered builds for machines without it.

points.title: Usage stats are a choice
points.text: On first launch ImHex asks whether to send anonymous usage statistics such as version, OS and GPU. You can change that in settings at any time, and crash logs go out only when you agree for that crash.

points.title: Mac builds are unsigned
points.text: The README asks for macOS 15 or newer and says release builds are unsigned, so you must allow them in Privacy and Security. Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because it fails the Gatekeeper check.

points.title: Free, with a verified Flatpak
points.text: ImHex is GPL-2.0, and its plugin library is LGPL so closed-source plugins are allowed. The Flathub package is verified as published by WerWolv. The Windows listing keeps 37 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
